description: The provided image displays three bar charts—labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4—each illustrating the relationship between perplexity and the number of quantization bits for two different methods: "Uniform" and "Ours." The vertical axis in each chart represents perplexity, with values ranging from 0 to 31 for (a) and (c), and from 0 to 410 for (b), with a consistent scale of 50 units between tick marks. The horizontal axis in all three charts is labeled "Quantization Bits" and features four discrete values: 3, 4, 8, and 16. For each quantization bit value, two bars are shown side-by-side: a dark blue bar representing the "Uniform" method and an orange bar representing the "Ours" method. In chart (a) WikiText, the "Ours" method consistently achieves a lower perplexity than the "Uniform" method across all quantization bit levels, with the difference being most pronounced at 3 bits (approximately 22 vs. 29). In chart (b) PTB, the "Ours" method also consistently outperforms the "Uniform" method, with a significant gap at 3 bits (approximately 250 vs. 400) and a smaller but consistent gap at 4, 8, and 16 bits. In chart (c) C4, the "Ours" method again achieves lower perplexity than the "Uniform" method at all tested quantization bit levels, with the performance gap being most noticeable at 3 bits (approximately 21 vs. 29). In all charts, the perplexity for both methods generally decreases as the number of quantization bits increases.
